Land area by elevation and climate-driven range shifts

geo-hypsometry.Rd

Tools for asking how much land a mountain offers at each elevation, and what warming does to the land available to species with known elevational ranges (Colwell et al. 2008; Elsen and Tingley 2015):

  • geo_hypsometry() gives the land area in each elevation band of a digital elevation model, optionally inside a region. Areas come from terra::cellSize(), so cells on a longitude/latitude grid are measured on the ellipsoid (area = "ellipsoid"), not as equal squares.

  • geo_range_shift() moves each species' range upslope by warming / lapse_rate and reports the land area within the range now and after warming, the percentage change, whether the shifted range no longer overlaps the current one (a gap, the range-shift gap of Colwell et al. 2008) and whether it runs past the summit (truncation).

  • geo_patches() labels connected patches of a mask and their areas; geo_largest_patch() keeps the largest, for example the main land mass of a peninsula once a valley floor has been cut out.

Usage

geo_hypsometry(
  dem,
  region = NULL,
  band_width = 100,
  area = c("ellipsoid", "planar"),
  unit = c("km2", "ha", "m2"),
  min_elevation = 0
)

geo_range_shift(
  hypsometry,
  ranges,
  warming,
  lapse_rate = 4.84,
  pad = 0,
  summit = NULL,
  lowland = NULL,
  floor = 0
)

geo_patches(
  x,
  min_area = 0,
  directions = 8,
  area = c("ellipsoid", "planar"),
  unit = c("km2", "ha", "m2")
)

geo_largest_patch(x, directions = 8)

Arguments

dem

Elevation SpatRaster (metres).

region

Optional area to keep: sf, sfc, SpatVector, or a SpatRaster mask (cells that are NA, FALSE or 0 are dropped).

band_width

Width of elevation bands in metres.

area

"ellipsoid" (true cell areas from terra::cellSize()) or "planar" (cell areas from the nominal resolution, only meaningful for projected grids).

unit

Area unit: "km2", "ha" or "m2".

min_elevation

Lowest elevation counted; cells below (sea, bathymetry, voids) are dropped. Default 0.

hypsometry

Result of geo_hypsometry().

ranges

Data frame of species ranges with columns species, lower and upper (metres).

warming

Warming scenarios in degrees C, for example c(1.8, 3.7) (IPCC AR6 SSP1-2.6 and SSP5-8.5, 2081-2100).

lapse_rate

Temperature lapse rate in degrees C per km. The default, 4.84, is a humid tropical value; give the one measured on your transect.

pad

Metres added below and above each observed range (an observed range underestimates the true one); lower limits are not padded below floor.

summit

Highest elevation available; defaults to the summit of the hypsometry. Shifted ranges are cut at the summit and flagged.

lowland

Species whose (padded) lower limit is at or below this elevation keep their lower limit (no area is lost at the bottom: there is no warmer land below them to vacate). NULL (default) shifts every lower limit.

floor

Lowest elevation (default 0, sea level).

x

A mask SpatRaster (cells that are NA, FALSE or 0 are background) or an elevation raster with NA outside the land.

min_area

Patches smaller than this (in unit) are dropped.

directions

8 (default, queen) or 4 (rook) neighbour cells.

Value

geo_hypsometry(): a tibble with one row per band: lower, upper, area, share (of the total) and area_above (land at or above lower), with attributes unit and summit (highest elevation).

geo_range_shift(): a tibble with one row per species and warming: species, warming, shift (m), lower, upper (padded current range), new_lower, new_upper, area_now, area_future, change (percent), gap (shifted range does not overlap the current range) and truncated (shifted range runs past the summit).

geo_patches(): a list with patches (a SpatRaster of patch ids, largest first) and areas (a tibble of patch and area). geo_largest_patch(): x with every cell outside the largest patch set to NA.

References

Colwell, R. K., Brehm, G., Cardelús, C. L., Gilman, A. C. and Longino, J. T. (2008). Global warming, elevational range shifts, and lowland biotic attrition in the wet tropics. Science, 322, 258-261.

Elsen, P. R. and Tingley, M. W. (2015). Global mountain topography and the fate of montane species under climate change. Nature Climate Change, 5, 772-776.

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("terra", quietly = TRUE)) {
  # A synthetic cone-shaped mountain, 0 to 3,000 m
  dem <- terra::rast(nrows = 100, ncols = 100, xmin = 145, xmax = 146, ymin = -7, ymax = -6)
  xy <- terra::crds(dem)
  terra::values(dem) <- pmax(0, 3000 - 6000 * sqrt((xy[, 1] - 145.5)^2 + (xy[, 2] + 6.5)^2))
  hyp <- geo_hypsometry(dem, band_width = 500)
  hyp
  ranges <- data.frame(species = c("a", "b"), lower = c(0, 1800), upper = c(900, 2100))
  geo_range_shift(hyp, ranges, warming = c(1.8, 3.7), pad = 250)
}
#> # A tibble: 4 × 12
#>   species warming shift lower upper new_lower new_upper area_now area_future
#>   <chr>     <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>       <dbl>
#> 1 a           1.8  372.     0  1150      372.     1522.    8527.       5736.
#> 2 b           1.8  372.  1550  2350     1922.     2722.    1777.       1131.
#> 3 a           3.7  764.     0  1150      764.     1914.    8527.       4095.
#> 4 b           3.7  764.  1550  2350     2314.     3114.    1777.        540.
#> # ℹ 3 more variables: change <dbl>, gap <lgl>, truncated <lgl>
# }
